judgment.rationale: The lock-screen/Windows Hello trigger is specific and a commenter confirms typing can make the cursor disappear, but neither report says whether moving the mouse after unlocking or disabling CursorHide restores it. Source behavior makes a stuck hidden cursor plausible; restoration failure and a secure-desktop cause are not established.
evidence: The report identifies PowerToys 0.102.2933 and cursor disappearance on the lock screen and some Windows Hello pages.

A commenter confirms typing a character on the lock screen makes the cursor disappear; they also recall rare Firefox/touchpad incidents without a reproducible sequence. No diagnostic attachment is provided.

At upstream main 9227a8497750, CursorHide hides on non-injected non-modifier keydown and restores after qualifying mouse movement; this matches the trigger but does not prove why it stays hidden: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/modules/MouseUtils/AutoHideCursor/AutoHideCursorState.h#L83-L109
judgment.recommended_action: Confirm post-unlock restoration behavior and exact CursorHide trigger setting

fix_assessment.rationale: A restoration problem is reported but its failing state transition is unknown. Ensure restoration after the reported sequence only if the behavior and setting are confirmed.

proposed_fixes.title: Restore the cursor after the confirmed lock-screen/Windows Hello trigger
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis only: CursorHide may enter its hidden state on keyboard input and fail to receive or act on a restoring pointer event across the lock/sign-in transition; no report confirms whether pointer movement or stopping the module restores it.
plan: Confirm the enabled hide-on-typing/idle option, exact sequence, and whether a deliberate pointer move or disabling CursorHide restores the cursor after unlock.
If the hidden state persists, trace the hide/restore transition across that desktop change and make restoration reliable without changing unrelated cursor settings.
verification: After the reported lock-screen/Windows Hello sequence, the cursor is visible again after unlock and normal pointer movement; disabling CursorHide restores the configured system cursor.

confidence.rationale: The source path fits the keypress trigger, but the exact restoration sequence and failing state are missing.

issue_context.summary: CursorHide can leave the pointer invisible after lock-screen keyboard input or Windows Hello activity, according to the report and one confirmation.
known_information: The original report identifies PowerToys 0.102.2933, lock screen, and some Windows Hello sign-in pages.
A commenter says a keypress on lock screen makes the cursor disappear and mentions rare Firefox/touchpad observations without a reproducible sequence.
inferences: The lock-screen keypress is consistent with the source hide-on-typing path but does not demonstrate a secure-desktop-specific defect.
The Firefox/touchpad observation may be a separate or intermittent trigger.
issue_context.analysis: The source hides on non-modifier keydown and restores on eligible mouse input, supporting investigation of the trigger. The missing discriminating fact is whether the hidden state survives unlock and ordinary pointer movement or whether ‘no return’ is limited to the secure desktop.
initial_investigation: Inspected AutoHideCursorState.h and AutoHideCursorWorker.cpp at upstream main 9227a8497750: keyboard and mouse hooks drive the transitions and pointer restoration uses a movement threshold: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/modules/MouseUtils/AutoHideCursor/AutoHideCursorWorker.cpp#L269-L307
Refreshed full issue body and only comment; no attachment. Focused lock-screen/CursorHide duplicate search did not surface a separate matching report.

information_gaps.information: Whether the cursor returns after unlocking and moving the mouse, whether disabling CursorHide restores it, and which hide-on-typing/idle option and pointing device were involved.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes a hidden state persisting across desktop transition from expected hide-on-typing behavior or a different intermittent touchpad/Firefox trigger.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: On the next occurrence, note the enabled option, press a key on the lock screen, then after unlocking try a deliberate mouse move and disable CursorHide; report which step restores the cursor and whether it happens with a touchpad, external mouse, or both.

comment.body: Thanks for confirming that a lock-screen keypress can make the cursor disappear, and for mentioning the separate rare Firefox/touchpad observation. After unlocking, does a deliberate mouse move bring the cursor back, and does turning CursorHide off restore it immediately? Please also say whether hide-on-typing, hide-on-idle, or both are enabled and whether the trigger occurs with a touchpad, external mouse, or both. Those details will show whether the hidden state persists across unlock or whether the reports have a different trigger.

actions.label: Review the conditional restoration direction
actions.note: Routing gate only; first confirm whether the hidden state persists after unlocking.
